detail: ASE 2023 pp.681-682 Table 1 footnote and Indications key points: abnormal cardiac screening results indicate fetal echocardiography independent of additional risk factors.
ASE p.682 Timing: fetal cardiology and obstetric teams determine the follow-up interval; wording does not introduce a requirement to decide together.
ASE p.687 abdominal situs: examine upper abdominal stomach liver aorta and systemic venous structures while attending carefully to fetal lie and transducer/display orientation.
ASE p.686 Figure 4 caption discusses examination of the fetal heart in orthogonal planes based on structural size thickness and orientation; not just a mandatory two-plane four-chamber view.
ASE p.690 Table 4: AV valve tricuspid and mitral annulus in early diastole is required as part of complete fetal echocardiography.

ASE pp.689 and 691-692: aortic and pulmonary annuli are required measurements. Timing remains internally inconsistent: prose/footnote favour systole but Table 4 row allows end-diastole or early systole.
ASE p.684 Image Optimization states the normal fetal heart-rate range in discussing frame-rate choice; the claim does not turn it into a separate optimisation threshold.

ASE p.698 Table 9 sinus bradycardia: any modality capturing simultaneous atrial and ventricular contraction; most ventricular rates exceed 90-100 beats/min. No added assertion of preserved AV conduction.
Wording matches ASE IV.B.i Imaging Tools for Assessing Fetal Cardiac Function on printed p.703. Change locator from p.702 to p.703; page 702 contains preceding material.
ASE p.718 Structural Heart Disease key points require aortic and ductal arch sidedness documented during every fetal echocardiographic examination.
ASE p.696 Table 8 early-gestation assessment: pulmonary and systemic vein assessment is limited; no stronger claim made.
ASE p.696 Table 8 early-echo imaging row: ALARA and thermal/mechanical indices at or below 1.0; soft-tissue TI before 10 weeks and bone TI from 10 weeks.
ISUOG 2023 p.789 Gestational age says many anatomical structures can be visualised satisfactorily beyond 22 weeks; it does not say specifically cardiac structures.
ISUOG p.793 Four-chamber view: small septal defects may be difficult to confirm with poor lateral resolution when fetal size and position are unfavourable.
